sn11.3:1.2: There it was that the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying:
sn11.3:1.4: “Reverend Sir!” those monks replied to the Fortunate One,
sn11.3:1.5: and the Fortunate One said this:
sn11.3:2.1: “Formerly, monks, there was a massed battle between the gods and the asuras.
sn11.3:2.2: Then, monks, the lord of the gods Sakka addressed the Tāvatiṁsa gods, saying:
sn11.3:3.1: ‘If, dear Sirs, to the gods who have gone into battle there should arise fear, or terror, or horror, at that time you could look for the top of my banner.
sn11.3:3.2: For to those who look to the top of my banner whatever fear there may be, or terror, or horror, will be given up.
sn11.3:4.1: If you cannot look to the top of my banner, then you could look for the top of the god-king Pajāpati’s banner.
sn11.3:4.2: For to those who look to the top of the god-king Pajāpati’s banner whatever fear there may be, or terror, or horror, will be given up.
sn11.3:5.1: If you cannot look to the top of the god-king Pajāpati’s banner, then you could look for the top of the god-king Varuṇa’s banner.
sn11.3:5.2: For to those who look to the top of the god-king Varuṇa’s banner whatever fear there may be, or terror, or horror, will be given up.
sn11.3:6.1: If you cannot look to the top of the god-king Varuṇa’s banner, then you could look for the top of the god-king Īsāna’s banner.
sn11.3:6.2: For to those who look to the top of the god-king Īsāna’s banner whatever fear there may be, or terror, or horror, will be given up.’
sn11.3:7.1: But, monks, to he who looks to the top of the lord of the gods Sakka’s banner, or who looks to the top of the god-king Pajāpati’s banner, or who looks to the top of the god-king Varuṇa’s banner, or who looks to the top of the god-king Īsāna’s banner, whatever fear there may be, or terror, or horror, may be given up, and may not be given up.
sn11.3:8.1: What is the reason for that?
sn11.3:8.2: The lord of the gods Sakka, monks, is not free from passion, is not free from hatred, is not free from delusion, being fearful, terrified, scared, he ran away.
sn11.3:9.2: ‘If to you, monks, after going to the wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty place, there should arise fear, or terror, or horror, at that time you could recollect me thus:
sn11.3:9.3: “Such is he, the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha, the one endowed with understanding and good conduct, the Happy One, the One who understands the worlds, the unsurpassed guide for those people who need taming, the Teacher of gods and men, the Buddha, the Fortunate One.”
sn11.3:9.4: For, monks, to those who recollect me whatever fear there may be, or terror, or horror, will be given up.
sn11.3:10.1: If you cannot recollect me, then recollect the Dhamma thus:
sn11.3:10.2: “The Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by the Fortunate One, it is visible, not subject to time, inviting inspection, onward leading, and can be understood by the wise for themselves.”
sn11.3:10.3: For, monks, to those who recollect the Dhamma whatever fear there may be, or terror, or horror, will be given up.
sn11.3:11.1: If you cannot recollect the Dhamma, then recollect the Saṅgha thus:
sn11.3:11.2: “The Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples are good in their practice, the Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples are upright in their practice, the Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples are systematic in their practice, the Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples are correct in their practice, that is to say, the four pairs of persons, the eight individual persons, this is the Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples, they are worthy of offerings, of hospitality, of gifts, and of reverential salutation, they are an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.”
sn11.3:11.3: For, monks, to those who recollect the Saṅgha whatever fear there may be, or terror, or horror, will be given up.
sn11.3:12.1: What is the reason for that?
sn11.3:12.2: The Realised One, monks, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha, is free from passion, is free from hatred, is free from delusion, not being fearful, not terrified, not scared, he did not run away.’”
sn11.3:12.4: and after saying this, the Happy One, the Teacher, said something more:
sn11.3:13.1: “In the wilds, at the root of a tree,
sn11.3:13.2: or in an empty place, monks,
sn11.3:13.4: and there will be no fear for you.
sn11.3:14.1: if you can’t remember the Buddha,
sn11.3:14.3: then you must remember the Dhamma,
sn11.3:14.4: which leads out, which is well preached.
sn11.3:15.1: If you can’t remember the Dhamma,
sn11.3:15.2: which leads out, which is well preached,
sn11.3:15.3: then you must remember the Saṅgha,
sn11.3:15.4: which is an unsurpassed field of merit.
sn11.3:16.1: Thus for those who remember the Buddha,
sn11.3:16.2: the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha, monks,
sn11.3:16.3: (there will be no) fear, or terror,
